items.text: Its members work to keep in place the existing system, in which public health coverage is guaranteed to older, disabled, and low-income residents, most others rely on employer or subsidized private insurance, and about 8 percent of residents have no coverage, voting against reducing it and for extending its subsidies.
Its members voted unanimously against a budget law that reduced funding for public health coverage for low-income residents, added work requirements to that coverage, and reduced food assistance.
Its members voted unanimously against a funding bill that did not extend the expiring premium subsidies.
Its members voted for a three-year extension of expanded premium subsidies for individually purchased health insurance.
A former chair of the group introduced, with more than 100 cosponsors, a bill to enroll every resident in a single public health plan with no premiums, deductibles, or copayments.
Adopted an official position, backed by a supermajority of its members, to oppose a funding deal because it did not extend the expiring premium subsidies.
Co-led a letter, joined by 208 legislators, telling the chamber's leader to drop any legislation that would cut the public pension or public health coverage for older or low-income residents.
Held a public hearing to build support for the single public health plan bill, where its chair called passing that bill one of the group's top priorities.
